context.projectOverview: One terminal vocabulary for SprintContract, and the rank-aware channel join — Two engines pick different words from the same enum for the same outcome — runSprintCycle writes "passed", PGE's sprint_exit writes "completed" — and five production readers filter for only one of them, so both MCP sprint tools return empty against a corpus of 250 contracts holding zero "passed". Standardise the word, give the readers a shared predicate so a third word cannot silently break them again, and replace the channel reducer's canonical-order duplicate resolution with the rank-aware join already shipping beside it. Closes two of the four conformance divergences.

completedSprints.title: One settled-status predicate
completedSprints.summary: isSettledContractStatus (passed|completed) + isTerminalContractStatus (adds failed) in src/contracts/sprint-contract.ts. Five readers + resume-cursor migrated. Relevant to sprint 4: the predicate is available if the join needs to be settled-status-aware.

completedSprints.title: No illegal contract statuses
completedSprints.summary: Four docs-correction contracts migrated pending->completed; run-time corpus guard in sprint-contract.test.ts.

completedSprints.title: A monotone version, replay-stable
completedSprints.summary: SprintContractSchema gained version?: number (optional, NO default). PGE sprintExitNode writes version: attempts (a count-filter over the appendById evaluations channel, hence order-invariant). 5 of 6 golden replay cases re-captured. Conformance field deltas went from three to FOUR (version: PGE writes it, ts engine does not).

contract.title: The channel join becomes rank-aware, and pipelineResult converges
contract.description: mergeEntries resolves a duplicate id by canonical order, under which every settled status sorts before the seeded "proposed" — so the channel keeps the planned copy and a pge run reports a contract still marked "proposed" inside completedSprints. Switch to the rank-aware join already shipping in the same module. This closes the pipelineResult divergence, so the two-directional pin must be edited deliberately here.

successCriteria.description: mergeEntries resolves duplicates with rankIsGreater rather than joinByCanonicalOrder. No new ranking logic is introduced — versionRank and rankIsGreater are reused exactly as they ship.
A test proves the settled contract outranks the seeded "proposed" one, so a pge run no longer reports "proposed" inside completedSprints.
The latent lastWriteWinsByKey defect is fixed and pinned: attempts:10 must outrank attempts:9, which canonical order got backwards.

ORDER-INVARIANCE IS PRESERVED — the property appendById exists for. A test merges the same containers in several different arrival orders and asserts an identical result. This is the criterion most likely to be broken silently by a ranking change.

The pipelineResult conformance divergence is CLOSED, and conformance.engines.test.ts's divergence-set pin and its per-field record are edited DELIBERATELY in the same commit as the docs/pge-graph.md disposition they change.
Any golden case whose recorded artifacts move is re-captured in THIS sprint, with the diff verified confined to the contract status/version and their direct consequences.
Full suite, typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green; golden gate passes with the replay count at or above its floor.

nonGoals: Weakening a pin to accommodate the change — the pin moves because the behaviour legitimately changed, and it must still fail in both directions afterwards.
Closing the contracts, history or audits divergences.
stopConditions: Order-invariance cannot be preserved under the rank-aware join — stop and report, because that property is why appendById exists.
A divergence other than pipelineResult moves — that is unplanned and must be understood before committing.
contract.definitionOfDone: All required criteria met, the full suite plus typecheck, typecheck:tests, lint and build green, the golden gate passing, and every documentation claim added backed by a test that fails when the claim stops being true.
contract.generatorNotes: The change itself is one line at reducers.ts:187. Everything else is proving it safe. rankIsGreater's total order is version, then updatedAt, then canonical JSON — the last term is what keeps it deterministic when the first two tie, which is what preserves order-invariance. Say in the code why that fallback matters. For sc-4-5, remember the discipline the previous spec established: a pin edit and the doc disposition it changes go in ONE commit, never as a side effect.
contract.evaluatorNotes: sc-4-4 is where a subtle break hides. Do not just run the generator's test — construct your own containers, shuffle them into several orders, and confirm identical results including when ranks TIE. Then verify sc-4-5 by reading the pin diff: it should record pipelineResult closing, not merely drop it. Confirm the divergence set is now exactly what a real run produces by running the harness yourself.

# Project Principles

> These principles guide all planning, generation, and evaluation in the Bober pipeline.
> Updated: 2026-04-16

## Mission

Agent-bober is a multi-agent harness that builds applications autonomously using any LLM. It orchestrates a pipeline of specialized agents (Researcher, Planner, Curator, Generator, Evaluator) and supports Claude, GPT, Gemini, and Ollama. It ships as an npm CLI + MCP server for Claude Code, Cursor, and Windsurf.

## Users

- **Primary:** Developers using Claude Code, Cursor, or Windsurf who want autonomous feature generation with quality gates
- **Secondary:** Teams integrating agent-bober programmatically via the TypeScript API or MCP server
- Technical level: intermediate to advanced — users understand LLMs, CI/CD, and modern JS tooling

## Quality Standards

- **Type safety:** TypeScript strict mode with all strict flags (`noUnusedLocals`, `noUnusedParameters`, `noImplicitReturns`, `noFallthroughCasesInSwitch`, `isolatedModules`). Zero type errors is a hard gate.
- **Lint compliance:** ESLint flat config with `consistent-type-imports` enforced, `no-explicit-any` warned, unused vars errored (with `_` prefix escape). Zero lint errors is a hard gate.
- **Test coverage:** Vitest for unit tests. Tests are collocated with source (`*.test.ts` next to `*.ts`). Tests run against the real project when practical (e.g., scanner tests scan agent-bober itself).
- **Build integrity:** `tsc` must produce clean output. Build is a required evaluator strategy.

## Technical Principles

### Follow

- **ESM everywhere.** `"type": "module"` in package.json. All imports use `.js` extensions for NodeNext resolution. No CommonJS.
- **Provider-agnostic interfaces.** All LLM interaction goes through `providers/types.ts` — provider-specific SDKs are wrapped by adapters (`anthropic.ts`, `openai.ts`, `google.ts`). Never leak SDK types outside adapter files.
- **Zod for config validation.** All configuration schemas are Zod schemas in `config/schema.ts`. Runtime config loading uses `z.parse()`. No hand-rolled validation.
- **Contract-based architecture.** PlanSpecs, SprintContracts, and EvalResults are the communication protocol between agents. They live in `contracts/` and are JSON files on disk in `.bober/`.
- **Filesystem state.** All mutable state (specs, contracts, handoffs, eval results, history) is stored as JSON files in `.bober/`. No database, no in-memory global state.
- **Section comments.** Use unicode box-drawing section headers: `// -- Section Name ------` to organize long files.
- **Small utility modules.** Utils in `utils/` are focused single-purpose files (`fs.ts`, `git.ts`, `logger.ts`). Keep them small.
- **Conventional commits.** Format: `type: description` where type is `feat`, `fix`, `docs`, `release`, `refactor`, `test`, `chore`. Sprint-generated commits use `bober(sprint-N): description`.
- **Use `type` imports.** ESLint enforces `consistent-type-imports` -- import types with `import type { ... }` syntax.
- **Prefix unused params with `_`.** The `_` prefix is the only escape hatch for unused variables/parameters.

### Avoid

- **No `any` without justification.** `no-explicit-any` is a warning; aim for zero. Use `unknown` + type narrowing instead.
- **No SDK lock-in.** Never import `@anthropic-ai/sdk` or `openai` outside of their respective adapter files in `providers/`.
- **No synchronous filesystem ops.** All fs operations use `node:fs/promises`. No `fs.readFileSync` etc.
- **No barrel re-exports for deep internals.** `src/index.ts` exports the public API only. Internal modules import directly.
- **No test mocks for filesystem.** Tests that need filesystem state create temp directories and clean up. The scanner tests run against the real codebase.

## Design Principles

N/A -- no user interface. Agent-bober is a CLI tool and programmatic library. The MCP server exposes tools, not UI.

securityDirective.source: sprint 3 security audit + adversarial verifier (both findings downgraded, but this directive is binding for sprint 4)
securityDirective.finding: materializeContracts' embedded branch (src/orchestrator/contract-materialization.ts:52-65) normalizes status, specId, sprintNumber and contractId on a producer-supplied contract but NOT version. SprintContractSchema bounds version only by .int().min(0) — no upper bound. Today this is inert because sprintContracts is bound to appendById and nothing reads SprintContract.version. It becomes decision-bearing the moment THIS sprint switches the join to consult versionRank: a seeded 'proposed' copy carrying an inflated version would permanently outrank the settled 'completed' copy — inverting exactly the ordering this sprint exists to provide.
securityDirective.required: Do not rank on producer-supplied version alone. Either (a) strip/reset version on the embedded branch of materializeContracts alongside the four fields already normalized there, or (b) make the join settled-status-aware so only a contract passing isSettledContractStatus may win on version. Pin whichever you choose with a test that fails if the guard is removed.
securityDirective.secondaryNote: If version ever becomes decision-bearing across a resumed/re-run boundary, derive rank from within-run state only — never trust a version read off disk. plan_materialize legitimately rewrites the contract file with the field absent (contract-materialization.ts:102-132), so the on-disk sequence can be 2 -> absent -> 1.
